newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.73 per dlr in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.73 per dlr in dull trade.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened to touch 35.73 in closing deals on Monday after trading in a tight range between 35.72 and 35.73 for most of the day, dealers said.

Dealers said late dollar purchases by a large state-run bank and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) led to the rupee's slight weakening in closing trade. The RBI bought dollars between 35.72 and 35.73 rupees per dollar, they said.
Dealers said there was little activity on Monday with many companies closed for Hindu New Year holidays. Banks in Bombay are closed on Tuesday for a local holiday.
"The holiday mood is still with us," a dealer at a state-run bank said. "Action should pick up on Wednesday."
"With RBI buying at 35.73, some players may be tempted to build long dollar positions," he added.
He said the rupee was likely to maintain current levels till month-end dollar demand picked up.
"It may then slip a bit," he said.
Dealers reported a quiet day in the forward market. The annualised premia for six-month dollars ended Monday at 6.54 percent against Friday's close of 6.49 percent, dealers said.
